clue.text: Unfeeling in a way to mention retiring

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word for mention is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite something is to mention it

explanation.surface: Someone cold and indifferent who mentions in passing that they are retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses the word for mention; 'in' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an apathetic person shows no feeling or interest.

clue.text: A strange plant

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd-looking plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the arum is a plant family including lords-and-ladies and the arum lily.

clue.text: Agrees with account over beheaded noblemen

indicators.note: over in a down clue means sitting above, so the abbreviation comes first
beheaded means the first letter of the word for noblemen is cut off

parts.note: lords are noblemen

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with an account of noblemen who lost their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops L from LORDS, leaving ORDS beneath ACC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to accord with something is to agree or be consistent with it.

clue.text: Gardening tool regularly available in chrome

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second letter of chrome

explanation.surface: A garden tool that comes in a chrome finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of CHROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding.

clue.text: King working in the queen's seat?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letters for king and working go within the word the

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A king busy at work in the queen's chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RON inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a queen sits on a throne, the question mark showing it belongs to any monarch.

clue.text: Arrange a test scan for sound generators

indicators.note: arrange means put in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A hospital sets up a test scan to check what makes certain noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' reorders the letters of A TEST SCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: castanets are clicking percussion instruments, so they generate sound.

clue.text: Sent back rotten fish

indicators.note: sent back tells us to write the word for rotten backwards

parts.note: rotten food is bad

explanation.surface: A diner returns a rotten fish to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' reverses BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dab is a small flatfish.

clue.text: Name key island Emirate

parts.note: to dub is to name
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Naming the key island in an emirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Dubai is one of the seven United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Ban on alien hereditary title

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ET is the alien of the film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A ban is placed on aliens holding inherited titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a baronetcy is a British title passed down from father to son.

clue.text: Difficult to understand relative with what's inside ears

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: what's inside points to the middle letters of the word ears, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A relative mumbles something muffled, as if there were something stuck inside one's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's inside' takes AR from the middle of EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unclear is obscure or hard to make out.

clue.text: Thus beer made half-heartedly is not drunk

parts.note: so means thus, as in 'and so'

indicators.note: half-heartedly says half of the heart of the word beer goes: one of its two middle letters is lost

explanation.surface: Weak, half-hearted beer means the drinker stays sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Es from BEER, leaving BER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sober person is free of intoxication.

clue.text: Talk with pensioner upset about tasteless articles

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the word for cheap goods
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of pensioner are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
tat is cheap, tasteless goods or trinkets

explanation.surface: A speaker talks while an upset pensioner complains about tacky goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the nine letters, and 'about' splits them so they surround the cheap goods; 'tasteless articles' is one idea, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a presentation is a formal talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Half of Saturday deemed to be very wet

indicators.note: half of means the first four of the eight letters of Saturday

parts.note: rated means judged or deemed to be

explanation.surface: Half of Saturday's weather was considered a washout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes SATU from SATURDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: saturated means soaked through.

clue.text: Eurozone's leader involved in nuisance with a former currency

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the initial goes within the word for nuisance

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Eurozone's

explanation.surface: The eurozone's head gets mixed up in an irritating row about an old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts E inside PEST to give PESET, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the peseta was Spain's currency before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Foretell proportional representation in advance of official order

indicators.note: in advance of means placed before, so the voting abbreviation comes ahead

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for proportional representation, a voting system
an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: Electoral reform is prophesied ahead of an official decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to predict is to forecast what will happen.

clue.text: Memorised Shakespearean role prior to National Theatre

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the role's name is placed ahead of the theatre's initials

parts.note: King Lear is the title role of a Shakespeare tragedy
NT is the abbreviation for the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: An actor learnt the part of Lear before taking it to the National Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Theatre is London's state-funded theatre, usually shortened to NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having learnt lines means having committed them to memory.

clue.text: Managed with playing card ordering

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a king is a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone ran a card game, sorting the cards by rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ranking is an ordering by position or merit.

clue.text: Three fail finally in stiff and correct entrance exam

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the final letters go within the word for prudish

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

indicators.note: finally points to the last letters of the words three and fail

explanation.surface: Three candidates fail a strict, proper admissions test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and L, and 'in' puts them inside PRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: a prelim is a preliminary examination, sat before admission or the main exams.

clue.text: Bold and imaginative Greens in trip for recycling

indicators.note: recycling means breaking something down and remaking it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners on a recycling trip show bold initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' rearranges the letters of GREENS IN TRIP; Greens as in green campaigners fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an enterprising person shows initiative and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Short lecture on form of bird's claw

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the last letter of the word for lecture is dropped

parts.note: a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: A brief lecture on the shape of a bird's claw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the final letter from the word for lecture; 'form of' is a loose link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Man-eating giant therefore returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the Latin word is read upwards in this down light

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A man-eating giant came back, therefore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses ERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in fairy tales an ogre is a giant who eats people.

clue.text: Small piece of land has a tenant?

definitions.meaning: a small island in a sea or river
a property that has a tenant is rented out, read as two words 'is' and 'let'

explanation.surface: An estate agent wonders whether a tiny patch of land has someone renting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words meaning 'is rented out'; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an islet is a very small island.

clue.text: Working lazily, not beginning to be inadequate

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the word for idling is dropped

parts.note: slacking means working lazily

explanation.surface: An idle worker is found wanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' removes S from SLACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lacking is deficient or falls short.

clue.text: Investing finally following company projection

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the final letter is placed after the abbreviation for company
finally points to the last letter of the word investing

explanation.surface: A company's projections follow from its investing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives G, placed after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cog is a tooth projecting from the rim of a gear wheel.

clue.text: Take the sun over in Anatolia

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters found are read backwards
in means the letters sit within the word Anatolia

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker sunbathes in Anatolia, in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds NAT within ANATOLIA, and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take the sun is to sunbathe, which makes skin go brown.

clue.text: Popular leader gambled over reversing EU move

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for gambled reads backwards

parts.note: gamed is an old word for gambled

indicators.note: reversing means the following letters for the union and a turn read backwards

parts.note: EU is the European Union
a go is a move or turn in a game

explanation.surface: A populist politician gambles on reversing a move by the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns GAMED into DEMAG; 'reversing' turns EU plus GO into OGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a demagogue is a leader who gains popularity by playing on prejudices.
